subject.title: trusted-proxy auth: support fallback/default user when identity header is absent

question: Should trusted-proxy auth accept a configured fallback/default identity when the request comes from a trusted proxy but the configured identity header is absent?
rationale: The requested behavior changes the Gateway auth trust boundary from per-request proxy-provided identity to operator-configured identity for headerless traffic, and repository policy treats fallback and auth/config surfaces as compatibility- and security-sensitive.

options.title: Keep fail-closed
options.body: Continue requiring the proxy identity header and document Cloudflare Zero Trust paths that do not forward identity on WebSocket upgrades as unsupported for trusted-proxy identity auth.

options.title: Add explicit fallback identity
options.body: Add a new trusted-proxy config field only with strict allowlist, required-header, origin/device-scope, audit, docs, and regression-test rules.

options.title: Use existing local password fallback only
options.body: Keep fallback limited to same-host direct callers with gateway.auth.password and require external browser/WebSocket traffic to preserve proxy identity headers.

recommendation.title: Keep fail-closed
recommendation.body: Continue requiring the proxy identity header and document Cloudflare Zero Trust paths that do not forward identity on WebSocket upgrades as unsupported for trusted-proxy identity auth.

likelyOwner.reason: The live issue is assigned to vincentkoc and the recent trusted-proxy origin-check work is in this same security boundary.
